titulo.texto: Walk: from the terraces to the hillside

frase_gancho.texto: A short stretch to listen to as you approach the rock.

puente_narrativo.texto: You have reached the slope of Cerro Chalcatzingo.

guion_corto.texto: The landscape changes here. Leave the terraces behind and approach the rock of the hill. So far you have seen monuments among houses and platforms, with themes of power. On the slope, according to David Grove, the great reliefs were carved on the living rock itself or on boulders at its base, and they speak of mythology and ritual. Those reliefs stand several meters apart, and you cannot see them all at once. To see them you have to walk, and perhaps that is how it was done in ancient times, in procession. When the path reaches the boulders, you are already in the next audio.

guion_largo.texto:
This is a walk. There is no need to stop. Leave the terraces behind and approach the hill while the audio keeps you company.

Up to here you have seen monuments among the houses and platforms of the settlement. Their theme, says Grove, is above all the political power of members of the elite. Many were found mutilated, decapitated or buried.

On the slope everything changes. The reliefs are carved directly into the rock of the hill or into large boulders at its base. They illustrate themes of mythology and religious ritual. The reliefs of the slopes were not mutilated the way those of the settlement were.

There is something else that makes this stretch special. The reliefs stand several meters apart and cannot be seen all together. To see them you have to move along the slope, and perhaps that is how it was done in the past, walking in procession.

When you reach the boulders at the base, you are already in the next audio.

texto: Look at the rock of the hill as you approach
Look for large boulders at the base
Walk slowly, as if in a procession

texto.Theme: from the settlement to the reliefs of the hill
